newsitem.title: UK: Dirty tanker trade slow, surplus tonnage build seen.
newsitem.headline: Dirty tanker trade slow, surplus tonnage build seen.

text.p: Dirty tanker chartering activity saw VLCCs continuing to find work in the key Mideast Gulf region for voyage East, but demand for Suezmax and Aframax tonnage in most regions was slower this week, brokers said.
"Although this week saw Halloween, charterers have not been too generous with their treats," one broker said.

Brokers E.A. Gibson estimated that despite steady bookings of around 28 VLCC type vessels out of the Mideast Gulf to the East this week -- a number comparable to last week -- there will be around 15.5 million tonnes of surplus tonnage between now and the end of November unless demand rapidly improves.
VLCC fixings to the U.S. Gulf took a steady W50 although trade in the direction has been fairly thin. Voyages to Singapore held W55 and South Korea and Japan valued around W57.

Transatlantic trade from West Africa saw slightly improved activity for million barrel tonnage which held around W92.5 for voyages to the U.S. Gulf, UKC and Med. Brokers said the fresh demand had helped take some of the pressure of Mediterranean markets where avails of Suezmax vessels are at a premium.

The Mediterranean market continued to see reasonable cross Med activity but brokers this market was nowhere near as busy as last week. Rates for Aframax tonnage slipped to around W105 off around 7-1/2 points since last Friday.
North Sea, Inter UKC trade for 80,000 tonne business fell around 30 points over the week to trade around W105 on Friday as more ships were shown to slowing demand from charterers.
"The party in the North Sea came to a rapid end," Brokers Galbraith's said in their weekly report.
Caribbean upcoast trade saw a fairly normal week's activity with rates a touch softer at around W120-W125 for USAC-Gulf voyages.
